jobs.occupation: Technical Project Manager - Data & Migration Team
jobs.description:
As our next Technical Project Manager in the Data & Migrations team, you will contribute to solving meaningful challenges across the life sciences industry. We offer specialised management consulting services, working with top-tier life sciences companies as well as biotech startups — locally and globally. From strategy development to hands-on implementation, we support our clients were impact matters most

About the role

This is a Senior role designed to provide program leadership to deliver strategic technical solutions that address complex client issues in the Life Sciences industry. As a manager within the Migration team, you will be handling projects and programs with regards to migration implementation to achieve desired outcomes and ensure successful business growth and regulatory compliance. You will also seek new business opportunities to help BASE life science grow its presence within existing and new customers.

You will provide program/project management oversight for all customer implementations falling under the Migrations team’s scope.

You will lead project teams consisting of data engineers/scientists. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in data engineering, project management and the ability to translate business requirements into technical specifications.

As a Technical Project Manager for the Migration team your responsibilities include:

• Monitoring program status including milestones, risks, issues, budgets, etc.

• Acting as a delivery escalation point and proactively ensuring escalations are handled promptly with a clear action and communication plan.

• Providing executive level summaries for senior executives in BASE life science.

• Intervening, when necessary, to ensure costs, timelines and quality are on track.

• Developed plans and effort estimates for future project during sales process.

Delivering Projects:

• Lead a cross-functional team to deliver data driven projects on time, within budget, and to the satisfaction of our life science industry stakeholders.

• Collaborate with business stakeholders in the life science industry to understand their data needs and translate them into technical specifications for the project team.

• Develop project plans, timelines, and budgets for the projects.

• Track and report on project progress, identifying and mitigating risks as needed.

• Facilitate communication and collaboration between the project team, life science industry stakeholders, and other teams within BASE life science.

What makes you the best person for this job?

• 5+ years of experience as a technical project manager ideally within the life science industry or other regulated areas.

• Successful track record of managing technically complex projects such as software development, implementation of IT systems, data migrations, etc.

• Experience leading developers, data engineers and/or data scientists and delivering data driven projects.

• Experience with project management tools such as JIRA.

• Experience with Agile project management methodologies such as SAFe.

• Strong communication skills, both in writing, meetings and in presentations.

• Strong verbal and written communication skills in English.

• A genuine interest in understanding the technical aspects of complex data-driven projects.

Additionally, the ideal candidate has the following qualifications:

• Experience with coding in Python, VBA, Java, R, SQL, C, or similar.

• Experience selling either projects or products to clients.

• Experience working with Veeva Vault.

This position is offered in Copenhagen, Denmark and Barcelona, Spain.

Who is BASE life science?

Founded in 2007, BASE life science is a business and technology consulting enterprise working exclusively in the life sciences industry.

With headquarters in Denmark and offices across Europe and the United States, we support clients globally. We work closely with our customers to identify, develop, and implement initiatives that drive growth, efficiency, and meaningful change. Through partnerships with leading solution providers such as Veeva, Salesforce, IQVIA, Benchling, and MediSpend, we help our clients unlock the full potential of modern technologies.

Why join BASE Life Science?

At BASE, you work on meaningful, complex challenges at the intersection of technology, science, and business. We trust our people with real responsibility and support them in turning ambition into impact.

You will be part of a collaborative, high‑performing environment where:

• Ambition is encouraged through ownership and continuous learning

• Execution matters — we focus on delivering solutions that work in practice

• Team spirit and trust guide collaboration across roles, countries, and disciplines

• Openness means your ideas are heard, you are challenged constructively, and supported as you grow

Alongside this, we offer:

• Support for health and wellbeing, covering physical, mental, and social needs

• Flexible ways of working, built on trust, autonomy, and balance

• A modern work setup, with the tools and equipment needed to do great work

We’re looking for a Senior Manager, Data & AI Architecture, based in Copenhagen or London, to lead our team of four Data, AI and Solution Architects and serve as the design authority for Pandora’s Data & AI platform. This is a genuine dual role. You’ll set the architectural direction and standards, while remaining close enough to the technology to challenge, review and approve the designs that matter.

Our target architecture is Databricks, including Delta Lake, medallion patterns and Unity Catalog, while Azure Synapse and its conformed enterprise models continue to power a significant part of the estate across supply chain, commerce, manufacturing, corporate technology and omni-channel.

A critical part of the role is leading the transition to Databricks: shaping the target architecture, determining where ownership sits as the platform evolves, and ensuring existing solutions remain coherent and supported throughout the journey.

The role is approximately 60% architecture and 40% people leadership. You’ll lead and develop four architects, but this is not a role where technical accountability is delegated to the team. Both sides of the role are real, and you’ll be expected to lead both.

Scope and authority

• Design authority for Data & Analytics: approves data and AI solution designs, and can require rework, attach conditions to an approval, or withhold approval.

• Chairs the architecture review forum, setting its standards, cadence and quality gates, and deciding what requires review against what is already covered by an approved pattern.

• Resolves conflicting design positions across architects, lead engineers and delivery teams.

• Owns reference architectures, solution patterns, data contracts and architecture decision records — accountable for their adoption, not just their publication.

• Owns the team's roadmap, capacity allocation across workstreams, and budget, including engagement of external consulting resources.

• Translates and enforces the Data & AI architecture strategy set by the Global Director, and informs how it evolves.

Job Responsibilities

Architecture

• Set and enforce the standards for what is built on Databricks as the target architecture, what remains on Synapse for now, and what is retired — and on what evidence.

• Decide how data products are aligned: source-aligned versus domain-aligned versus consumer-aligned, where ownership and stewardship sit, and where a conformed enterprise model (CDM/RDM) serves better than distributed ownership.

• Review technical designs from solution architects and lead engineers against platform standards; give feedback that changes the design, not just documents it.

• Define and evolve reference architectures, solution patterns and data contracts so that quality is built in rather than inspected in.

• Lead design sessions with architects, engineering and business stakeholders on complex or contested problems.

• Oversee transitional architectures through to legacy decommission, maintaining business continuity and closing the parallel run.

AI architecture

• Set and enforce architecture standards for agentic systems: orchestration, tool and data access boundaries, evaluation, guardrails and observability.

• Set and enforce architecture standards for ML systems: feature reuse, training and serving topology, model lifecycle, and monitoring for drift.

• Approve AI solution designs with enough depth to arbitrate them on the technical merits, and in line with AI policy and applicable regulation.

Governance and regulation

• Embed privacy-by-design and personal data handling requirements into platform patterns, particularly across commerce and omni-channel.

• Maintain computational governance: data quality frameworks, contracts and lineage as platform capability rather than project effort.

Team leadership

• Line management for four architects: coaching, performance, career development, hiring.

• Establish ways of working — review process, documentation standards, quality gates — and hold the team to them.

• Represent architecture in leadership forums, steering committees and cross-functional planning.

• Keep architects hands-on and embedded with engineering teams; architecture produced at a distance from delivery does not land.

What you will have done by month 12

• A published and adopted standard for what is built on Databricks, with evidence of designs changed by it.

• A clear model for data product alignment and ownership, applied on live work rather than documented in isolation.

• An architecture review forum running to a predictable cadence, with a visible ADR record and a known path for challenging a decision.

• Approved agentic and ML reference patterns in use.

• At least one legacy component fully decommissioned, not just superseded.

• A development plan in place for each of the four architects, and any open roles filled.

Essential experience

jobs.description:
Calling all ambitious and curious students to join Deloitte’s Mentor Programme 2027 – a unique programme for finance and economics students interested in consulting.

Are you excited about Finance Operations and Transformation? Do you wish to gain insights into the life of a consultant within the CFO area? Would you like to advance your personal and professional growth journey through exclusive sparring sessions with a mentor from Deloitte?

Then apply now for a spot in our Mentor Programme 2027!

The Mentor Programme 2027

Deloitte’s Finance Transformation (FT) department is at the heart of the Mentor Programme, offering engagement opportunities for students with an interest in Finance Transformation. Our FT team, consisting of +350 consultants based in Copenhagen and Aarhus, supports clients by operating, advising, optimising, and managing finance functions. The work spans all areas under the CFO, including operational finance, finance optimisation, ERP implementation, performance management, and finance strategy. We collaborate with a broad range of private and public clients, including C25 companies and key public institutions, both nationally and internationally.

As part of the Mentor Programme, you will be invited to educational workshops and social events that will provide you with deep insights into our toolbox and life as a consultant. These events provide great opportunities to network with Deloitte professionals and fellow peers.

Throughout the programme, you will receive personalised guidance through 1:1 sessions with a mentor from Deloitte. These sessions are aimed at guiding you towards your personal and professional ambitions and goals. Topics touched upon with your assigned mentor can cover everything from student life, courses, and bachelor/thesis topics to career sparring and dialogues around CV and applications. The mentor-mentee relation is centred around your development, whereas you will be the one to choose the topics that are most relevant for you to discuss.

The Mentor Programme runs from January to September 2027. Throughout the course of the programme, we have arranged four main events that we expect you to commit to attending*:

• Event 1, ultimo January: The Beginning | Introducing the Programme & Deloitte

• Event 2, primo March: Opening our Toolbox | Strengthening Your Skills

• Event 3, ultimo April: Unique Insights | Explore & Engage

• Event 4, ultimo August: Festive Culmination | Celebrating the Finalization of Your Journey**

In addition to the main events, we will arrange smaller group sessions with 3-4 mentees and mentors. These sessions will allow you to network in a more personal setting and gain deeper insights into areas such as client projects and tools.

* The event dates are subject to change, and the final dates will be provided later.

** All events are held in the evening and start at 16:00 earliest.

We embrace students on their bachelor’s and 1st year master’s degree with interest in all aspects under the CFO’s responsibilities.

The Mentor Programme 2027 is centred around Finance Transformation. However, a few mentors from two other departments are represented and involved in the programme. This involves the following:

• Strategy & Performance (Monitor) is Deloitte’s strategy practice that combines deep industry insights with cutting-edge methods to help leaders resolve their most critical decisions, drive value, and achieve transformational success. We specialise in end-to-end strategy consulting, helping chief executives and their teams solve their most complex problems by advising on everything from growth and corporate strategies to operating models and cost and capital optimisation. We deliver tailored solutions that ensure long-term success and efficiency for our clients.

• Corporate Finance Advisory is part of Deloitte’s dedicated M&A practice, guiding clients through every stage of the transaction lifecycle – from identifying targets and buyers to structuring deals and realising post-close value. We support a diverse range of clients, including corporates, private equity firms, financial investors, and family-owned businesses. Our integrated service offering span sell- and buy-side advisory, debt capital advisory, and complex financial modelling. By combining deep industry expertise with rigorous financial analysis, we enable leaders to navigate complexity, structure optimal deals, and unlock sustainable value - creating an impact that matters.

In case you are interested in joining the Mentor Programme with a mentor from one of the abovementioned departments, please select this in the application form. Please note that Finance Transformation is the main department represented, hence the largest proportion of mentors and mentees will be within Finance Transformation.

Be aware that Strategy & Performance (Monitor) is only represented in Aarhus, while Corporate Finance Advisory is represented in both Aarhus and Copenhagen Mentor Programme 2027.

How to apply

To ensure that all participants obtain maximum value from the Mentor Programme 2027, we have limited number of seats. To apply for the programme, you must attach your CV and grade transcript, as well as answer the following screening questions in the sign-up form:

• Why do you wish to participate in the Mentor Programme?

• Which experiences and competences do you bring into the network?

• What are your career ambitions and key strengths for your future career?

We expect to get back to you shortly after the application deadline. If you are selected to proceed in the application process, you will receive an invitation to a short online interview about your motivation.

Apply now to seize the opportunity to unleash your potential and expand your network.

Deadline: Sunday November 1, 2026.

Contact

If you have any questions, you are welcome to reach out to our mentor coordinators:

Katrine Hjenner Rasmussen (Copenhagen)

ahjenner@deloitte.dk

Phone: + 45 3093 6297

Ditte Marie Jørgensen (Aarhus)

dittemariej@deloitte.dk

Phone: + 45 2970 6613

In Deloitte, you will find passionate, caring people who are curious by nature and striving to evolve. We value our different skills, perspectives and experiences and foster an environment where innovative powers thrive. To us, success is the feeling that the work we are doing will outlast us. The impact we make is not about what we achieve as individuals, but how we enable those around us to be their very best. From professional development to leadership opportunities, we empower our people to be extraordinary by playing to their strengths – because that is how we can make a difference.

Hemab is building preventative treatments for serious, underserved bleeding disorders. These therapies are designed to work with the body's own biology and stop bleeds before they start, instead of treating them after they happen. We're patient-first, science-led and clinical-stage, with a pipeline that takes different scientific approaches to different patient needs.

We went public via our 2026 IPO, and we're scaling across two homes: Cambridge, MA, USA, and Copenhagen, Denmark.

The role

As Director, Medical Writing, you will be dedicated to one of our compounds under clinical development, taking ownership of the clinical and regulatory writing that helps move this compound through development. You will turn complex clinical and scientific evidence into clear, accurate documents that regulators can act on - connecting the science, data and development strategy into one coherent story.

This is a hands-on role. You will write, shape and drive documents yourself while bringing physicians, scientists, biostatisticians and regulatory colleagues together around high-quality outputs and demanding timelines.

What You'll Do At Hemab

• Own medical writing for one of our leading compounds, from document strategy and planning through drafting, review and finalization.

• Lead development of clinical documents, including clinical study protocols, clinical study reports, Investigator’s Brochures, and clinical submission documents appropriate to the program’s stage.

• Contribute to clinical content of regulatory and safety documents, such as briefing documents, regulatory responses, and DSURs.

• Translate complex clinical and statistical data into clear, scientifically accurate narratives for regulatory reviewers.

• Partner closely with clinical development, regulatory, biostatistics, safety, and other scientific colleagues to align document content with the program strategy.

• Drive cross-functional document reviews, resolve comments constructively and build alignment without compromising scientific accuracy.

• Apply relevant regulatory requirements and guidance, including ICH E3, ICH E6 and applicable FDA and EMA expectations.

• Build writing plans and practical frameworks that keep interdependent documents moving against development and submission timelines.

• Maintain document quality, consistency and version control while adapting quickly as data, priorities and timelines evolve.

• Identify writing or documentation risks early, take ownership of solutions and give the program team a clear view of what is needed next.

• Collaborate with internal cross-functional teams and external vendors to manage public disclosure activities in compliance with transparency rules.

What You'll Bring to Hemab

Essential:

• Bachelor’s degree or higher in a scientific discipline, with at least 10 years of hands-on medical writing experience in biotechnology, pharmaceutical or CRO clinical research environments.

• Significant experience authoring clinical and regulatory documents across drug development.

• Strong working knowledge of ICH E3, ICH E6 and relevant FDA and EMA requirements.

• Scientific fluency and the ability to interpret clinical trial data and statistical outputs accurately.

• Excellent written English, with the ability to make complex science clear, structured and precise.

• Strong cross-functional communication skills and experience bringing multiple expert reviewers to alignment.

• Ability to own competing documents and deadlines independently while maintaining quality.

Nice to have

• Advanced scientific degree such as an MS, PhD or PharmD.

• Medical writing certification or relevant regulatory affairs training.

What to expect, honestly

Hemab is still building a lot of its own structure. You'll create some of the writing frameworks you need rather than inherit a finished system. We work across Copenhagen and Cambridge and priorities can move quickly as clinical data and development plans change.

You'll need to solve problems when you reach the first wall rather than pass them on. That means taking ownership, asking for help when you need it, working without ego and being comfortable making progress when every answer isn't available yet. At a company our size, how you work matters as much as pedigree. Good structure should help people move faster and trust the work, not slow them down.

Why Hemab

Your writing will sit close to the point where clinical science becomes a potential treatment for patients. People living with serious bleeding disorders have spent too long reacting to bleeds after they happen. We're working to give them the chance to prevent them.

How we treat our people is meant to be an extension of how we think about patients: with care, honesty and respect. We want the same from our hiring experience - transparent, human and clear from first conversation to final answer.

Hemab builds balanced candidate slates and assesses everyone against a single standard. Reasonable adjustments are available at any stage of the hiring experience.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Hemab Therapeutics is proud to be an equal opportunity employer, seeking to create a welcoming and diverse environment. All applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, creed, gender, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, pregnancy, sex, marital status, gender expression or identity, genetic information, sexual orientation, citizenship, or any other legally protected class.

Do you enjoy writing C++ software that interacts directly with hardware and makes complex systems perform reliably in the real world?

At Robotto, we build advanced autonomy and software solutions for drones and unmanned systems. Our work brings together computer vision, embedded software, control, electronics and real-world product development.We are looking for an Embedded Software Engineer with strong C++ experience to develop software close to the hardware layer of our drone platform. Experience with motor control and Field-Oriented Control (FOC) is highly preferred.This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys working at the intersection of software, electronics and control systems, where performance, reliability and real-world behaviour matter.

The role
You will work on embedded software that supports the control and operation of Robotto’s drone and unmanned systems.Your work will involve developing reliable C++ software that interfaces with hardware, sensors, motors and other system components. You will work closely with colleagues across control, electronics, computer vision and flight testing to take software from development through integration and into real-world operation.For candidates with motor-control experience, you will also have the opportunity to contribute to the development and improvement of our motor-control capabilities, including Field-Oriented Control (FOC).

What you will do

• Develop and maintain embedded software in C++ for drones and unmanned systems.
• Build software that interfaces with motors, sensors, actuators and other hardware components.
• Work with real-time and performance-sensitive software.
• Contribute to motor-control software, including Field-Oriented Control (FOC), where relevant to your experience.
• Develop and integrate communication between embedded components and wider product systems.
• Debug complex software and hardware interactions and identify root causes of issues.
• Collaborate closely with control, electronics, flight-test and software engineers.
• Contribute to software architecture, testing, documentation, code quality and technical decisions.
• Support integration and testing on real hardware and drone platforms.
What success could look like in your first 3–6 months

• You have developed a strong understanding of Robotto’s embedded architecture, hardware and control systems.
• You are contributing production-quality C++ code to our embedded platform.
• You are successfully integrating and debugging software on real hardware.
• You are contributing to improved reliability and performance across our embedded systems.
• If you have motor-control experience, you are actively contributing to our FOC and motor-control development.
• You have become a trusted technical partner for colleagues across software, control, electronics and flight testing.
What we are looking for
We are looking for an engineer who is comfortable working close to hardware and enjoys solving complex technical problems where software and physical systems meet.

• At least 3 years of professional software engineering experience, ideally within embedded or real-time systems.
• Experience with motor control, particularly Field-Oriented Control (FOC), is highly preferred. Experience with BLDC/PMSM motors, control loops, PWM, encoders or related motor-control technologies would also be highly relevant.
• Strong C++ programming skills.
• Hands-on experience developing software that interfaces with hardware.
• Experience with embedded systems, real-time systems, microcontrollers or similar low-level environments.
• Good understanding of debugging, testing, software architecture and version control.
• Experience with communication protocols such as CAN, UART, SPI, I²C or similar is an advantage.
• Experience with robotics, drones, autonomous systems or other complex electromechanical products is an advantage.
• Professional fluency in English.
• A degree in computer science, software engineering, electrical engineering, robotics, mechatronics or a related field is preferred; equivalent practical experience is equally welcome.
Who you are
You are practical, curious and comfortable getting close to both the software and the hardware when solving a problem.

• You take ownership of your work and care about software quality and reliability.
• You enjoy understanding how systems behave beyond the code itself.
• You approach debugging methodically and are comfortable solving difficult software/hardware problems.
• You collaborate well across software, electronics and control disciplines.
• You are comfortable working in a fast-moving environment with evolving priorities.
• You communicate technical trade-offs, progress and risks clearly and pragmatically.
Minds and makers forging ahead together.
At Robotto, we value people who do. People who take ownership, are willing to try new things just to see if they work, and are comfortable asking for forgiveness rather than permission. We want people who are curious, proactive and excited about turning ideas into something real.

Our hiring process
Our process is designed to be straightforward, practical and conversational:

1. Introductory conversation with our Talent Acquisition & Recruitment Partner
A chance to learn more about Robotto, the role and what you are looking for, while giving us an opportunity to understand your background and motivation.

2. Meeting with the Hiring Manager / Principal Engineer
A deeper conversation about your technical background, C++ and embedded experience, motor-control experience where relevant, and your approach to solving engineering problems.

3. In-depth Technical Evaluation & Meeting with our COO
A hands-on technical session where you will receive a short assignment to prepare in advance and then work through it together with members of our technical team, similar to a pair-programming exercise. The focus is on understanding your technical approach, problem-solving and how you collaborate.Following the technical evaluation, you will meet with our COO for a conversation about the role, Robotto and mutual fit.

4. Offer
If there is a strong mutual fit, we will move forward with an offer.

Why join Robotto?
Robotto is building advanced autonomy technology for drones and unmanned systems, working at the intersection of software, hardware, computer vision, control and real-world operations.You will join a highly technical and ambitious team at an exciting point in the company’s journey. As we continue to scale our engineering team and work on challenging new projects, you will have the opportunity to influence how our embedded and control software develops.This is a role where your software will not remain behind a screen. You will see it integrated with real hardware, tested on real systems and used in demanding real-world environments.You will work closely with talented engineers, take meaningful technical ownership and help shape the next generation of Robotto’s technology.

Equal Employment Opportunity
Robotto is committed to providing equal employment opportunities and fostering an inclusive workplace. We recruit based on skills, experience and potential. Please note that certain positions may require specific nationality or eligibility for security clearance in accordance with applicable laws and the nature of our work.
